definition: Making digital assets withstand physical hazards: towers and masts reinforced for wind and seismic loads, equipment raised above flood levels, flood-proofed and hardened shelters and housings, armoured, buried or aerial cable chosen for local hazard exposure, and climate-resilient design of data centres (raised floors, flood barriers, redundant cooling).

Choosing where digital assets go using hazard and climate risk information: siting towers, data centres, landing stations and cable routes away from flood, landslide, storm-surge and coastal erosion zones, elevation and setback requirements.
note: Not a seed activity of its own: drawn from A031, A036 and A044.

definition: Ensuring one failure does not cut service: ring or mesh fiber topology, a second or geographically diverse submarine or terrestrial route, multiple transmission paths (fiber, microwave, satellite) and automatic rerouting.

Keeping digital assets powered when the grid fails: battery banks, diesel, solar or hybrid generators for cell sites, data centres, internet exchange points, emergency operations centres and health facility systems.

measure_name: Data backup, disaster recovery sites and failover
definition: Keeping data and services recoverable: geographically separate backup data centres or cloud, mirrored databases, automatic failover, offsite backup of registries and records, data embassy or multi-cloud arrangements.

Plans for running digital services and networks through a disruption, and testing them: business continuity and disaster recovery plans for government systems, national emergency telecommunications plans, priority routing and coordination with disaster management.

Communications that keep working for responders and warnings when public networks fail: redundant links (fiber, satellite, radio) for emergency operations centres and warning dissemination, pre-positioned satellite equipment, standby satellite service agreements.

Rules and arrangements that let networks back each other up: operators sharing towers, fiber and spectrum during emergencies, emergency roaming when a provider fails, open access and fiber pooling including fiber on power lines (OPGW).

measure_name: Resilience standards and climate risk screening
definition: Building resilience into design and procurement: climate and disaster risk screening of investments, resilience design standards, and resilience requirements written into bidding documents, contracts and public-private partnership agreements.

measure_name: Climate vulnerability assessment of digital infrastructure
definition: Assessing and mapping how exposed digital assets are: assessments of current and projected climate risk to telecom and data infrastructure, mapping of assets against hazard data for resilience planning.
Reducing dependence on single equipment suppliers so capacity can be maintained and restored: vendor diversification and strategic reserves of spare components.
note: may be out of scope as not climate-related.
